summary: Introductory intake to understand Maple Ridge's security and hosting constraints. Main concerns: BYOK/KMS integration, SSO/SAML and SCIM provisioning, audit log ownership & retention, SOC 2 / ISO evidence, and whether Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private meets data residency and latency needs. Agreed next step: share compliance artifacts and schedule technical deep dive to scope pilot.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-31
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Evan Cole (Head of Platform - Maple Ridge), Maya Lin (Security Engineer), Raj Patel (CTO)

Auto-generated summary (may be imperfect): Intro call to gather security posture and hosting requirements, explore Redwood hosting modes (hosted, dedicated, private) and KMS/SSO constraints.

[00:00] Jesse Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick intros — I'm Jesse, AE at Redwood Inference. Priya is our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Evan Cole: Hey — Evan here. We'll mostly be talking to Maya and Raj for security and architecture.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Hi all. Priya: I focus on private/dedicated deployments and integrations like KMS and SSO.
[00:25] Raj Patel: Thanks. We're evaluating options to host LLM inference for our product — latency sensitive, lots of PII, and strict retention rules.

[00:40] Jesse Martinez: Great. High level, we're hoping to map out requirements: SOC 2 / ISO posture, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and any VPC or data residency constraints. Then propose a pilot.
[01:05] Maya Lin: Right — to add color: we need to know whether Redwood Hosted can meet our compliance, or if we must do Dedicated or Private. Also BYOK is a hard ask from our security team.
[01:27] Priya Shah: Understood. We support Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem). For KMS — we have options: Redwood-managed keys, customer-managed keys in cloud KMS, and an HSM-backed option for Private deployments. There are tradeoffs; I can walk through them.
[01:54] Raj Patel: Can you clarify BYOK for hosted? We prefer keys we control, but hosting might not allow BYOK.

[02:10] Priya Shah: Short answer: for Hosted, we offer envelope encryption with Redwood-managed keys by default. We do have a BYOK path for Dedicated with customer KMS integration (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS) where keys are in the customer's account and we use cross-account roles. Fully air-gapped on-prem with HSM is available in Private deployments. There's sometimes a minor latency/ops overhead for key wrap/unpack for every model load; we can show numbers in the pilot.
[02:48] Maya Lin: That latency detail is important. Our SLAs target 200–250ms median for inference.
[03:00] Priya Shah: Makes sense — if you need that SLA, Dedicated with smart routing and local GPUs in your region is a common pattern. Hosted can hit sub-200ms for smaller models but can be less predictable during bursts. We'll capture your latency distribution in the benchmark.

[03:30] Evan Cole: On audits: We need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 evidence. Do you provide reports or a rights to audit?
[03:40] Jesse Martinez: We can share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO summary. For enterprise customers we also do targeted questionnaires (we completed an external ISO audit last cycle) and can work on a SOC bridge letter if needed.
[03:56] Maya Lin: Good. Also for RBAC — we want admin separation, delegated roles for model deployment vs ops vs billing, and SCIM provisioning.
[04:12] Priya Shah: Redwood RBAC supports layered roles — org admins, project owners, deployers, billing viewers. SSO via SAML and OIDC is supported; SCIM provisioning works with Okta/OneLogin. For Dedicated and Private we can integrate with your IdP for network-restricted SSO.
[04:36] Raj Patel: How are audit logs handled? Are they stored by Redwood or can they be pushed to our SIEM? Retention?
[04:46] Priya Shah: We retain operational logs (routing, API calls, token-level counters) by default for 90 days on Hosted. For enterprise/Dedicated you can configure longer retention and export via streaming to S3, Kafka, or direct SIEM ingestion. Private deployments let you keep logs entirely in your environment.
[05:08] Maya Lin: We need 1-year retention for API-level audit logs and 7 years for certain compliance traces. Also need guaranteed immutability for some records.
[05:18] Jesse Martinez: Okay — immutability is doable in Private or Dedicated with customer-side object lock on S3; Hosted may be trickier but we can provide write-once buckets in your account for exported logs. We'll note that as a requirement.

[05:40] Evan Cole: Data residency — we have EU customers so residency in eu-west is required for certain workloads. How flexible are your regions?
[05:50] Priya Shah: We host in multiple regions and can pin deployments to regions. Dedicated pools can be created in particular cloud regions. For Hosted you can set routing preferences, but exact region guarantee for multi-tenant Hosted is limited. Private gives full control.
[06:10] Raj Patel: Encryption at rest — besides KMS, what about model weights and KV cache encryption?
[06:20] Priya Shah: Model artifacts and weights are encrypted at rest. KV cache is stored in a secure cache tier and is encrypted; for Dedicated we can configure the cache to use customer-managed encryption keys. For Private, everything stays within your VPC and storage accounts.
[06:41] Maya Lin: Are tokens or prompt text logged by default? We have to avoid storing raw PII.
[06:49] Priya Shah: By default we collect telemetry and token counts. Persistent storage of prompts/output in Hosted is opt-in. For Dedicated/Private you control whether to persist raw inputs; we support no-logging modes and prefix/KV caching only in memory. We'll map the no-PII requirement in the pilot design.

[07:10] Evan Cole: Does Redwood provide a data processing agreement and standard contractual clauses for EU data transfer?
[07:18] Jesse Martinez: Yes — DPA with SCCs is supported for enterprise contracts. We'll share a draft.

[07:30] Raj Patel: About SSO: We use Okta, need SCIM provisioning and Just-in-Time group syncing. Any limits?
[07:40] Priya Shah: Okta SCIM provisioning is supported. Group sync frequency and JIT provisioning are configurable; for high-scale orgs we have guidance to avoid rate-limiting. We can provide SCIM endpoints and sample configs.

[08:00] Maya Lin: Logging format — is it JSON with structured fields? We want to map fields into Splunk.
[08:08] Priya Shah: Yes — audit logs are structured JSON with metadata (user, api_key, model_id, latency_ms, inputs_hashed when configured). We provide a docs sample for Splunk/Datadog/Elastic ingestion.

[08:30] Jesse Martinez: Let's talk about incident response and breach notification — what's your policy?
[08:37] Priya Shah: Redwood has an incident response runbook; for enterprise we commit to a 72-hour initial notification and post-incident report. We also support SOC-level contacts and runbook integration.
[08:50] Maya Lin: Do you offer penetration test reports or allow third-party pentest on dedicated/private infra?
[08:57] Priya Shah: We can share our internal pen-test summaries. For Dedicated and Private customers, we provide a process to arrange customer-led assessments in scoped windows — typically with an approval flow and a pre-agreed scope.

[09:20] Evan Cole: On the technical side — if we pick Dedicated, what are the provisioning lead times and scaling options?
[09:28] Priya Shah: Provisioning for Dedicated typically takes a few days for standard configs; for specific GPUs or private regions it can be longer. Autoscaling policies support burst capacity to handle spikes; we'd discuss expected throughput to size pools.

[09:50] Raj Patel: We have a concern: for BYOK with AWS KMS, does Redwood get access to keys during model serving or is it transparent?
[09:59] Priya Shah: With customer KMS, keys live in your account. Redwood uses temporary cross-account roles to unwrap keys as needed; you control key policies and can rotate keys. We can support envelope encryption so the long-lived keys are never exposed to Redwood staff.

[10:20] Maya Lin: What about auditability of key usage? We need CloudTrail logs showing each decrypt/unwrap operation.
[10:28] Priya Shah: Yes — the unwrap events appear in CloudTrail in your account. We'll provide an architecture diagram showing key flow and logging configuration.

[10:40] Evan Cole: Are there differences in billing visibility and cost breakdown between Hosted and Dedicated?
[10:47] Jesse Martinez: Hosted is usage-based with token/embedding unit billing. Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract with detailed per-token/offload billing and cost dashboards in the Redwood Console. Billing visibility is more granular for Dedicated.

[11:05] Raj Patel: For the pilot, we want to test with a 7B model and an LLM-embedding workflow. Can Redwood support that in Dedicated with our KMS and VPC peering?
[11:15] Priya Shah: Yes — that's a common pilot. We'll design a two-week benchmark: latency p50/p95, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, and verify KMS/SCIM/SIEM integration. We'll need sample prompts and a small traffic replay to simulate load.

[11:45] Maya Lin: Regarding data deletion — if we cease service, can we get a certified wipe of persistent caches and logs?
[11:54] Priya Shah: Yes — for Dedicated/Private we perform certified deletion in coordination with your team and provide attestation. For Hosted we can schedule data purges and provide export of logs before deletion per contract.

[12:10] Evan Cole: Do you support role-level restrictions to prevent certain users from invoking models or exporting embeddings?
[12:18] Priya Shah: Role-based controls allow limiting access at project and route level. You can also set policy-based restrictions on which models are available in an environment.

[12:40] Jesse Martinez: Quick clarification on timelines — if we do a pilot, what does success look like from your perspective?
[12:47] Priya Shah: For us: validated latency and throughput targets, successful KMS integration with required audit trails, SSO/SCIM working for test users, and log ingestion into your SIEM. Then we scope Dedicated sizing and contract.

[13:05] Raj Patel: Sounds good. Any concerns on Redwood's side with our retention asks (1 year API logs, 7 years for compliance items)?
[13:14] Priya Shah: No major blockers; we recommend Dedicated with log export to your S3 with object lock for long-term retention. We'll outline the architecture for immutable archives.

[13:40] Evan Cole: Are there any showstoppers around model weights residency? We need weights to be in EU for some workloads.
[13:49] Priya Shah: We can pin model artifacts to EU regions in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, multi-tenant model hosting might cache weights in several regions — for strict residency, Dedicated is preferred.

[14:10] Maya Lin: For the technical deep dive, we'd like a session that includes network diagrams, KMS flow, and a demo of log export into our Splunk test environment.
[14:18] Priya Shah: We'll prepare that. Priya: I'll include a network diagram, KMS unwrap flow with CloudTrail examples, SCIM sample payloads, and a step-by-step for SIEM export.

[14:35] Jesse Martinez: Final quick recap and owners? Jesse will share SOC2/ISO docs. Priya will scope the pilot and schedule the technical deep dive. Maya will share retention windows and SIEM endpoints. Raj/Evan will align procurement timeline.

[14:55] Raj Patel: Procurement — we are aiming for a pilot start in mid-April and a contract decision by end of May, assuming pilot OK.
[15:05] Jesse Martinez: Good — we'll target those dates. Any other questions?
[15:12] Maya Lin: One last item: do you support customer-supplied instrumentation for additional tracing?
[15:18] Priya Shah: Yes — we provide tracing hooks and can send trace spans to your tracing backend with secure connectors. We'll include examples.
[15:28] Jesse Martinez: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and link to schedule the tech deep dive.

[15:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription quality: occasional speaker overlaps and minor misrecognitions (e.g., KV becoming K V cache) may appear.
